mainTopic: Why a slave is acquired with land only if he stands in it; then whether קדשים קלים count as the owner's property for damages, following רבי יוסי הגלילי
overview: Before this amud, a ברייתא taught that slaves sold together with land are acquired along with the land only if they stand in it. The גמרא asked why, whether a slave counts as land (שמואל's rule for distant fields) or as movable property (no piling needed). It answers that things which move by themselves are different. A slave is 'land that walks', and שמואל's rule works only because all the earth is one connected block. Then the גמרא turns to the משנה's phrase נכסים שאין בהן מעילה and infers that it refers to consecrated property that simply has no מעילה. רבי יוחנן explains that this means קדשים קלים, following רבי יוסי הגלילי, who holds they are the owner's money. A משנה about קידושין is answered by saying this applies only while the animal is alive, not after שחיטה. Then a משנה about selling a בכור, as limited by רב נחמן to nowadays, raises a new difficulty. רבא challenges רב נחמן, and רבינא answers that the case is a בכור from חוץ לארץ. The amud ends as the גמרא starts a new question built on these ideas, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Movable property does not need to be piled on the land
steps.stepSummary: The challenge to the view that a slave counts as movable property: we already hold that movable property acquired along with land does not need to be piled up on that land.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we hold that movable property does not need to be piled up on the land!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge. If a slave counts as movable property (מטלטלי), why must he stand inside the land to be acquired with it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that movable items can be acquired along with land even if they are not lying on that land. A slave under this view is just a movable item. So the ברייתא's demand that the slaves stand in the field seems to contradict the accepted rule.

keyTerms.meaning: But we hold / it is established for us (introduces an accepted rule)
Piled up (movable items gathered on top of the land)

phrases.english: But we hold
that we do not need [movable property] piled up [on the land]!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קַיְימָא לַן דְּלָא בָּעֵינַן צְבוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the challenge begun before this section, now aimed at the view that a slave is like מטלטלי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's requirement that slaves stand within the land, under the view that a slave is movable property.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Movable property acquired with land does not need to be on the land, so a slave who counts as movable should not need to stand there either.

steps.title: Things that move by themselves are different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that movable things which walk on their own (slaves) are different from movable things that stay put. The 'no piling needed' rule only covers things that stay put.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what must you say? Movable property that moves around is different from movable property that does not move around.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the answer that anyone would have to give for the מטלטלי view. It uses a 'what else could you say?' opening, and this sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An object like a bag of grain stays wherever it is. A slave can walk away, so he is a special kind of movable property. For him, the rule that items need not be piled on the land does not apply, so he must stand in the field.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what do you have to say? (what answer would you be forced to give?)

phrases.english: Rather, what do you have to say?
Movable property that moves around is different
phrases.notes: He means things that walk on their own, like a slave.

phrases.english: from movable property that does not move around;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by splitting movable property into two types.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (חילוק) between movable things that move by themselves and those that do not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All movable property follows one rule, so a slave need not stand in the field.
steps.terutzMaskana: Self-moving property like a slave is different and must be within the land to be acquired with it.

steps.title: A slave is land that walks, unlike real fields
steps.stepSummary: Using the same idea, the גמרא answers the challenge against the view that a slave is like land. A slave is 'moving land', while שמואל's rule only works for fields, since the earth's crust is one block.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, land that moves around is different from land that does not move around. A slave is land that moves around. There, in שמואל's case, the crust of the earth is all one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the 'things that move are different' idea and uses it for the other view, that a slave is like מקרקעי. So both challenges are answered the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל taught that acquiring one field can acquire distant fields too. That works only because all ground is one connected piece of earth. A slave is not attached to the ground, so he cannot be joined to the land that way, and he must stand in it.

keyTerms.meaning: The base or crust of the earth (the ground as one solid block)

steps.whatToRemember: Under both views of a slave (like land or like movables), he must stand in the field to be acquired with it, because he walks on his own. שמואל's rule for distant fields works only because all ground is one connected earth.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a single idea, that something which moves by itself is different, solving two separate challenges at once.

phrases.english: Here too, land that moves around is different
from land that does not move around.
A slave is land that moves around,
[but] there, the crust of the earth is one.
phrases.notes: 'There' means שמואל's case of acquiring many fields in different places.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the distinction from step 2 to the other view (slave is like land), answering the challenge from שמואל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Parallel distinction (חילוק): land that moves versus land that does not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If a slave is like land, שמואל's rule for distant fields should let him be acquired without standing in the field.
steps.terutzMaskana: A slave is 'moving land' and is not part of the one connected earth, so שמואל's rule does not cover him.

steps.title: New phrase from the משנה: property with no מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה: one is liable for damage only to property that has no מעילה. The next step reads closely what this wording includes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Property that has no מעילה, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the slave discussion and quotes a new line of the משנה. This sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה limits damage liability to property that has no מעילה. It does not simply say 'property that is not הקדש', and the next step builds on that wording. The 'and so on' shows that only the opening words of the משנה are quoted here.

keyTerms.meaning: Misusing הקדש (holy property) for personal use, which brings a penalty
And so on (the rest of the quote is understood)

phrases.english: Property that has no [liability for] misuse of holy property, and so on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic; no direct link to the slave discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Damage liability applies only to property that has no מעילה.

steps.title: Inference: The Property Is Consecrated, Just Without מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה's wording closely. 'No מעילה' implies the property can still be consecrated, and yet one pays for damaging it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The only thing missing is מעילה. But the property is still הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the words of the משנה it just quoted. This sets up the next question about who holds this view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה could simply have said 'property that is not הקדש.' Instead it said 'property without מעילה.' That suggests there is consecrated property that has no מעילה, and the משנה still makes the damager pay for it.

keyTerms.meaning: The sin of using הקדש (property belonging to the Temple) for personal benefit

phrases.english: It is only מעילה that they do not have,
but they are consecrated;

steps.triggerLanguage: מְעִילָה הוּא דְּלֵית בְּהוּ, הָא מִקְדָּשׁ קָדְשִׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the wording of the משנה quoted in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the משנה, consecrated property that has no מעילה is still covered for damages.

steps.title: Who Is the תנא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that consecrated property can count for damages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the view inferred in the last step. This sets up רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually הקדש belongs to Heaven, not to a person, so it would not count for personal damages. The גמרא needs to know whose opinion allows consecrated property to still count as a person's property.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (which sage of the משנה period taught this)?

phrases.english: Who is the tanna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the view inferred in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that consecrated property without מעילה still counts for damages?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: קדשים קלים, Following רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the משנה is about קדשים קלים and follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who holds they are the owner's money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: the משנה is talking about קדשים קלים, and it follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who says they are the owner's property.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question. The consecrated items in the משנה are קדשים קלים, and the משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קדשים קלים have no מעילה while they are still alive. According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, they still belong to the owner, so damaging them hurts the owner's money and the damager must pay.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of lesser holiness, such as a שלמים
A תנא who holds that קדשים קלים are the owner's property

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
It is about offerings of lesser sanctity –
and according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
who says: it is the property of the owner.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי and is about קדשים קלים, which he considers the owner's money.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the damages משנה to one specific opinion. That is why a source that seems to argue with רבי יוסי הגלילי becomes a problem next.

steps.title: The ברייתא Showing רבי יוסי הגלילי's View
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from the פסוק that קדשים קלים are a person's own money.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: 'And commits a trespass against ה׳' comes to include קדשים קלים, which are his own property. These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source showing that רבי יוסי הגלילי really holds that קדשים קלים are the owner's money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about someone who swears falsely that he does not have his friend's item. רבי יוסי הגלילי says the rule also covers denying a friend's קדשים קלים. That only makes sense if those offerings are still that friend's own money.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: As it is taught: “And commits a trespass against the Lord” –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:21. This פסוק is about someone who denies holding his friend's item and swears falsely.

phrases.english: to include offerings of lesser sanctity
which are his property,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the view of רבי יוסי הגלילי cited in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that קדשים קלים are the owner's money.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading ויקרא 5:21 as including קדשים קלים, since they are his property.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוסי הגלילי, קדשים קלים still belong to their owner. That is how the damages משנה can make someone pay for harming consecrated property.

steps.title: Challenge: A כהן Cannot Betroth with His Portion of קדשים קלים
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says a כהן cannot betroth a woman with his portion of any offering, even קדשים קלים. Does that משנה disagree with רבי יוסי הגלילי?
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned: one who betroths with his portion, whether of the most holy offerings or of קדשים קלים, the woman is not betrothed. Shall we say that משנה does not follow רבי יוסי הגלילי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי הגלילי's view with a משנה about קידושין. A כהן's portion of even קדשים קלים is not good enough to betroth a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To betroth a woman, a man must give her something that is his own money. If קדשים קלים are the owner's money, a כהן's portion of them should work, but the משנה says it does not. That makes it look as if this משנה argues with רבי יוסי הגלילי.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn in a משנה?
His portion (a כהן's share of an offering)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two meanings of the root קדש here. 'המקדש' means betrothing a woman, not making something holy. 'קדשים' means holy offerings.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:
One who betroths with his portion,
phrases.notes: He means a כהן giving a woman his share of an offering's meat.

phrases.english: whether with offerings of the most sacred order
or with offerings of lesser sanctity –
she is not betrothed.
Shall we say this is not in accordance with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the view of רבי יוסי הגלילי established in steps 7–8, using a משנה in קידושין.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי הגלילי's view (relied on by רבי יוחנן) that קדשים קלים are the owner's money.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Betrothal requires the man's own money. The משנה rules that a כהן's portion of קדשים קלים cannot betroth, which implies it is not his money. That seems to contradict רבי יוסי הגלילי.

steps.title: Before slaughter it is the owner's; after slaughter it is from God's table
steps.stepSummary: Even רבי יוסי הגלילי only says קדשים קלים are the owner's money while the animal is alive. After שחיטה he agrees the כהנים receive their share from God's table, so a כהן cannot use it for קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say the משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי. He said 'owner's money' only about a live animal. After slaughter, even he agrees that the כהנים receive their portion from the table of the Most High.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 9. There is no disagreement between the קידושין משנה and רבי יוסי הגלילי, because they are talking about different stages of the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי's ownership rule covers the live animal only. Once it is slaughtered, the כהנים eat as guests at God's table and do not own the meat. Something you do not own cannot be used for קידושין, so the קידושין משנה fits his view.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say (this follows that view)
From the table of the Most High (God)

steps.confusionAlert: Being allowed to eat something is not the same as owning it. The כהנים may eat the meat, but in this answer they do not own it.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows Rabbi Yosei HaGelili;

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי – מֵחַיִּים,
phrases.english: when Rabbi Yosei HaGelili said it, that was about while the animal is alive,
but after slaughter,
even Rabbi Yosei HaGelili agrees,
that when they receive it,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the כהנים getting their portion of the offering.

phrases.english: they receive it from the table of the Most High.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 by splitting before and after שחיטה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction by stage: live animal versus slaughtered animal
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קידושין משנה seemed to argue with רבי יוסי הגלילי's view that קדשים קלים are the owner's money.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי הגלילי only means the live animal. After שחיטה the כהנים eat from God's table, so they cannot betroth with it.

steps.title: Is a live offering really the owner's? The firstborn משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether even a live animal counts as the owner's money. It brings a משנה that a כהן may sell a בכור and betroth with it. That source becomes a challenge once it is paired with רב נחמן's comment in the next step.
steps.simpleTranslation: And while it is alive, does he really say so? But we learned: a בכור may be sold alive if it is unblemished, and alive or slaughtered if it has a blemish, and one may betroth a woman with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the split it just made, asking whether even the live animal is the owner's money. It quotes a משנה about a בכור, setting up the next step, which explains how this משנה is limited.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats a בכור, which is a type of קדשים קלים, as the כהן's property, since he can sell it and use it for קידושין. On its own, that seems to support ownership while the animal is alive. The real challenge comes from how רב נחמן limits this משנה, which is the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And while alive, does he really say so?
But didn't we learn in a משנה?
Firstborn male of a kosher animal, given to the כהן

phrases.english: And while it is alive, does he really say so?
But didn't we learn: a firstborn animal,
one may sell it when it is unblemished
while alive (and not when slaughtered),
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets and some don't. Either way, an unblemished בכור may only be sold alive.

phrases.english: and a blemished one, alive or slaughtered.
And one may betroth a woman with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the 'while alive' half of the answer in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that קדשים קלים are the owner's money while the animal is alive
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It brings the בכור משנה, which together with רב נחמן's limitation suggests that ownership of a live offering is not so simple.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the firstborn is the כהן's only nowadays
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, limits the בכור משנה to today, when the animal cannot be offered. When the בית המקדש stands, the כהנים do not own it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: this was taught only about a בכור nowadays. Since it cannot be offered, the כהנים own it. When the בית המקדש stands and it can be offered, they do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב נחמן's limitation of the בכור משנה. This is what turns the משנה into a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רב נחמן's reasoning, a live offering that can still be brought on the מזבח is not the כהן's property. That goes against the claim that רבי יוסי הגלילי counts live קדשים קלים as the owner's money. This sets up רבא's objection in the next step.
steps.whyThisMatters: It makes ownership depend on whether the animal can actually be offered right now.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּכוֹר בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה –
phrases.english: They taught this only about a firstborn nowadays,
since it is not fit to be offered,
phrases.notes: There is no בית המקדש, so the בכור just waits until it gets a blemish.

phrases.english: the priests have ownership of it;
but when the Temple is standing,
when it is fit to be offered, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge of step 11 by limiting the בכור משנה to nowadays.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן owns a בכור only when it cannot be offered (nowadays). When the בית המקדש stands, he does not own it while it is still fit to be offered.

steps.title: רבא objects to רב נחמן from רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן with רבי יוסי הגלילי's ברייתא, which counts קדשים קלים as the owner's money. That ברייתא speaks of a time when the בית המקדש stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected to רב נחמן: 'And commits a trespass against ה׳' comes to include קדשים קלים, which are his own money. These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's limitation by quoting the ברייתא from step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק makes a person who falsely denies holding the animal bring a קרבן אשם, which only applies when the בית המקדש stands. Even so, רבי יוסי הגלילי calls קדשים קלים the owner's money, and these animals can still be offered. That contradicts רב נחמן's claim that animals fit for offering are not owned.

keyTerms.meaning: And he raised an objection to him
And commits a trespass against ה׳‎ (ויקרא 5:21)

phrases.english: And Rava raised an objection to Rav Nachman:
"And commits a trespass against the Lord"
comes to include offerings of lesser sanctity, which are his own property,
the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili!
phrases.notes: This is the same ברייתא quoted back in step 8.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's statement in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's rule that קדשים fit for offering are not owned
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי הגלילי's ברייתא speaks of a time when the בית המקדש stands, since it involves a קרבן אשם. Yet it calls קדשים קלים the owner's money even while they can be offered.

steps.title: רבינא says the ברייתא is about a בכור from outside the Land
steps.stepSummary: רבינא defends רב נחמן. רבי יוסי הגלילי's ברייתא speaks of a בכור from חוץ לארץ, following רבי שמעון. Such a בכור should not be brought to the מקדש in the first place, so the כהן owns it even while the בית המקדש stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא answered: the ברייתא is talking about a בכור from outside ארץ ישראל, and it follows רבי שמעון. He says: 'If they came unblemished, they are offered.' His words show that if they already came, yes, they are offered. But nobody should bring them in the first place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers רבא's challenge from step 13. He shows that רבי יוסי הגלילי's ברייתא can fit with רב נחמן's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said a כהן owns a בכור only when it cannot be offered, as is true today. רבינא points out that a בכור from חוץ לארץ is also not meant to be offered: according to רבי שמעון, we only offer it if it already arrived. So even when the בית המקדש stands, this animal is like today's בכור, and the כהן owns it. The ברייתא no longer contradicts רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male animal, given to a כהן
From the outset; the proper way to act in the first place

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון does not say a בכור from outside the Land is unfit if it arrives. It IS offered if it already came. The point is only that no one should bring it in the first place, and that is enough to treat it like a בכור that cannot be offered.

phrases.english: And Ravina answered:
It is about a firstborn outside the Land [of Israel],
and it follows Rabbi Shimon, who says:
If they came unblemished, they are offered.
If they came, yes,
but from the outset, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge against רב נחמן from step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא is set in a specific situation, a בכור from חוץ לארץ.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי הגלילי seemed to say the owner owns a בכור even when the בית המקדש stands and the animal can be offered, against רב נחמן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a בכור that should not be brought to be offered at all. That matches רב נחמן: the כהן owns a בכור only when it is not meant for the מזבח.

steps.title: Setting up a question: if רבי יוסי הגלילי means only while the animal is alive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new question. It takes for granted that רבי יוסי הגלילי's 'it is his property' applies only while the animal is alive. The rest of the question comes in the next part of the daf.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is true that when רבי יוסי הגלילי said 'it is his property,' he meant only while the animal is alive...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It restates a starting point about רבי יוסי הגלילי so it can build a question on it in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10 we learned that רבי יוסי הגלילי calls קדשים קלים the owner's money only while alive, not after שחיטה. רבינא has just shown that רב נחמן's limit also fits רבי יוסי הגלילי. The גמרא now begins to ask what follows from putting these two ideas together. The actual difficulty is not stated yet.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it is so (opening a question that builds on an assumption)

phrases.english: And if it is so
that when Rabbi Yosei HaGelili said
'it is his property,' it was about while it is alive,
phrases.notes: This is the idea from step 10: after שחיטה, even רבי יוסי הגלילי agrees it is not the owner's.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אִיתָא דְּכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי מָמוֹנוֹ הוּא מֵחַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבינא's answer (step 14), which treats רב נחמן's limit as true even for רבי יוסי הגלילי. It combines this with the 'only while alive' idea from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The way רבי יוסי הגלילי's view is now being understood: owner's money only while alive, and only when the animal cannot be offered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only the setup appears here. The גמרא states the assumption that the challenge will be built on, and finishes the question in the next part of the daf.
